headline_finding: P-01 V2 (risk-limited continuous conductance controller) materially outperforms B (existing predictive closed-loop) on 4 of 5 attack modes. V2 captures 100% of oracle benefit on 4/5 attacks. The mechanism is genuinely different from existing art (rate limiting + drainage floor + alpha floor + hysteresis). V2 weakness: sensor dropout (35% oracle capture) and multi-failure (peak 224 mmHg, catastrophic but 2x better survival than B).

P-01.summary: Built V2 controller (10_V2_comparison.py, ~700 lines). V2 extracts R279 failure lesson ('hard isolation is fragile; soft modulation is robust') as a design constraint and adds 4 mechanisms: (1) rate-limited alpha changes (max 2%/sec, prevents abrupt transients), (2) drainage floor (min 50% of target, prevents collapse), (3) alpha floor (min 5%, no hard isolation), (4) hysteresis (3% deadband, reduces valve wear). Ran 4 arms (A simple / B predictive closed-loop / C V2 / D oracle continuous) × 5 attacks (none, noise_3x, fast_occlusion, sensor_dropout, multi_failure) × 1 seed = 20 runs. V2 beats B on 4/5 attacks: none (3.6x), noise_3x (4.3x), fast_occlusion (4.4x), sensor_dropout (1.3x). V2 captures 100% of oracle on 4/5 attacks. Weakness: sensor_dropout (35% oracle), multi_failure (peak 224 mmHg but 2x survival vs B). 1-seed result — multi-seed confirmation required before bench validation.
